newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on Brazil rains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on Brazil rains.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on Friday, pressured by rains in Rio Grande do Sul that smoothed fears of drought-related crop losses, traders said.
"It's follow-through liquidation with a rain event to help the short side," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Rains alleviated dryness in Brazil's key soybean growing region of Rio Grande do Sul but were holding up harvesting progress in Mato Grosso, Brazilian growers said.
Funds largely bailed out the March contract after it fell eight cents per bushel to $7.33-1/2, which technical traders pegged as a second support level.
Refco Inc bought eight million bushels of March. Prudential Securities, R.J. O'Brien, O'Connor and CO and Iowa Grain were also among the buyers, traders said.
Commercials were also small-lot players on both sides of the market. Cargill Inc, Continental Grain, FCC and Produce Grain were said to be on both sides.
In options trade, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer bought 1,000 March $7.25 calls at 18-1/2, traders said.
Soybeans closed down 5-1/4 to 3-1/4 cents per bushel with March off 3-1/4 at $7.38-1/4.
Volume was estimated at 50,000 contracts, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 53,352 contracts, according to CBOT data.
